text:
B: Hiya! Oh, hello, can you hear me? I'm Joanne.
A: Yeah, I can hear you. Kerry.
B: Lovely to meet you, Kerry. Where are you based?
A: Bridgwater, Somerset. You don't have to do the posh voice, you know.
B: Ha! Am I doing it? It's the phones, sorry. Eight hours a day of it. I'm Warrington, me, nothing posh about it.
A: That's better. What do you do then?
B: I'm a team leader in a contact centre, broadband and TV. Eleven on my team. Mostly retentions, so when people ring up to cancel we keep them.
A: Oh, so you're the ones who won't let you go.
B: Guilty! But it works both ways. We knock a bit off, they're happy, we're happy. Everyone wins, do you know what I mean?
A: Except they always put it back up after a year. My mum's went up twelve quid last year and she didn't even notice till I looked at her bank.
B: Erm, well, to be fair, that's all in the terms. It's not us that sets the prices, that's upstairs. What is it you do yourself?
A: Tills and the customer service desk at a supermarket. I had a woman kick off at me today over a ten pence coupon.
B: Oh my God, I'd have just given it her. Give it me, I'd say, and stuck it through anyway.
A: Well I wouldn't. It'd run out. Rules are rules, if I let her, the next one wants it, then the next.
B: No, you're right, you're right. I'm the same with my team, you can't give an inch. Are you a manager there, then?
A: No. They asked about team leader. I couldn't be doing with the paperwork.
B: Oh, you'd be good though. You've got that, you know, nobody's going to mess you about. That's half the job.
A: Maybe. What's your weekends like, then?
B: Rugby, me and Gary have got Wolves season tickets. Or nights out, bottomless brunch in Manchester with the girls. I've just booked Lanzarote for October, actually.
A: I did Tenerife once. Too hot. Full of English people moaning anyway.
B: Oh, you want a nice hotel, that's the trick, a good pool bar. I always chat the rep up for an upgrade. Where do you go instead?
A: Caravan at Brean. It's twenty minutes away and you can read the menu.
B: Aw, I love that. Simple. Nothing wrong with simple. Have you got your tea on tonight?
A: My dinner, yeah. Sausage and mash. Reduced sausages, forty pence.
B: Get you! See, that's clever, that. Gary does a fry-up on a Saturday, sausage on a barm, bit of brown sauce...
A: A what?
B: A barm. A barm cake. A bread roll.
A: Oh, for God's sake. I've had cob twice today and now barm. It's a roll! Why can't any of you just say roll?
B: Ha! Who said cob?
A: The teacher, and that electrician. He told me I was wrong.
B: Well, he's wrong, it's a barm. Don't let him tell you otherwise. Have you got kids, Kerry?
A: Callum, seventeen. Mechanics at college.
B: My Kieran's an apprentice sparky, twenty-three. They grow up so fast, don't they? He comes round for his tea every Sunday though, can't get rid of...
